title: Decay series
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches a decay series: the radioactive decay point covers radiation types and the isotopes point covers isotope definitions, and neither shows an unstable isotope decaying step by step to a stable one.

draft.title: Decay series
card: Some unstable isotopes do not reach a stable nucleus in one decay. The product may also be unstable, so it decays again.
A decay series is this chain of decays, one step after another. It ends when a stable isotope is formed.
A decay series diagram plots mass number A against atomic number Z. Each isotope is a point, and each decay is an arrow to the next.
An alpha decay lowers A by 4 and Z by 2. A beta-minus decay keeps A the same and raises Z by 1. This shows which decay each arrow stands for.
draft.remember: A decay series is a chain of decays that stops only at a stable isotope.

a.q: What happens at the end of a decay series?
opts: A stable isotope is formed and decay stops
The nucleus breaks into single protons
All the radiation stops after one decay
The atomic number returns to its first value
a.why: The chain continues while each product is unstable, and stops at a stable isotope. One decay is not always enough, so it is wrong to say the series ends after one step.
a.clue: Think about when a nucleus has no reason to decay again.

b.q: On a decay series diagram, an arrow goes from A = 214, Z = 84 to A = 210, Z = 82. Which decay does the arrow show?
b.why: A falls by 4 and Z falls by 2, which matches an alpha particle. Beta-minus would leave A unchanged and raise Z by 1.
b.clue: Compare the change in A and the change in Z with each decay.

a.best: A stable isotope is formed and decay stops

check.summary: No problems found. The arrow from A = 214, Z = 84 to A = 210, Z = 82 matches Po-214 alpha decaying to Pb-210, so both intended answers are correct.
